title: Cups-browsed migration: locale-safe empty queue and CUPS-down
head: 4d2ea3d06f23
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new CUPS-down guard cannot read the normal saved queue file and treats that failure as no queues
leads.consequence: Omarchy migrations run as the desktop user, but a previously started Arch CUPS writes /etc/cups/printers.conf root:cups 0600. grep exits 2, is silenced and falls through like a match-free file. The script removes cups-browsed and writes both machine and user completion markers even with implicitclass queues still saved. Once CUPS starts these queues need the removed backend, and the guard is not retried. Do not interpret an unreadable file as empty: use a safe privileged read or fail pending on read errors, then distinguish a genuinely absent file.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); corroborated, published

leads.summary: #12503 merges textually but its scheduler-down alternative shadows this PR's new guard
leads.consequence: The other open PR adds Scheduler is not running. to the first elif. The three-way merge is syntactically clean but selects the earlier elif before the new grep, so a readable saved discovery URI is treated as empty and cups-browsed is removed/marked. Both PRs' stated scheduler-down handling cannot safely coexist as-is; reconcile the condition if both are merged.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); corroborated, published

leads.summary: A missing printers.conf can still conceal CUPS-restorable queue definitions
leads.consequence: If the active printers.conf is absent but its .O backup survives an interrupted configuration save, grep returns nonzero and the migration removes the backend and marks done. CUPS itself reads printers.conf.O if printers.conf does not exist and can restore the saved implicitclass queue when restarted. Treat absent differently from confirmed empty, check the CUPS recovery path or leave pending until CUPS can list queues.
leads.triage: Opus final noted it as rare edge not worth acting on; not published

leads.summary: The substring search mistakes printer descriptions or comments for a saved discovery queue
leads.consequence: For a readable config whose only implicitclass:// text is an Info field or comment, the scheduler-down branch claims discovery queues remain and exits 1. No package removal or markers occur; omarchy update aborts before post-update tasks and later migrations and the login notifier repeatedly offers a retry until CUPS comes up or the unrelated text changes. Match DeviceURI implicitclass:// in a printer record, not any substring. Stock 0600 permissions normally mask this false positive by causing H1 instead.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified cups printers.c:1508 Info and :1525 DeviceURI written as separate lines; folded into suggested anchored pattern as one sentence

leads.summary: The unconditional comment about cups-browsed leaving queues behind does not hold on Arch's shipped default
leads.location: migrations/1788009111.sh:19-21 (unchanged premise relied on by this follow-up)
leads.consequence: For graceful shutdown with CUPS reachable, Arch cups-browsed 2.1.1 compiles with KeepGeneratedQueuesOnShutdown=No and attempts deletion of idle generated queues itself. The migration still matters for down CUPS, queued jobs, failed deletion, crashes and custom Yes, but the comment and any explanation that all stopped services leave queues overstate the normal case. No change to the down-branch defect H1 is implied.
leads.triage: pre-existing unchanged base comment, outside this follow-up's change; R1 already noted leftovers are uncommon; not published

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12101#issuecomment-5856500919) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12101#issuecomment-5857409852), checked at head `4d2ea3d0`. The comment fix is resolved. The new CUPS-down check does not take effect on real systems, because it cannot read `printers.conf` as the user migrations run as.

| Earlier point | At `4d2ea3d0` |
|---|---|
| Comment credited `LANGUAGE` instead of `LC_MESSAGES` | Resolved |
| Scheduler-down completes without checking saved discovery queues | Still present in effect (new check below) |
| Overlap with open PR #12503 | Changed: no merge conflict now, but merging both disables the new check |
| Description links closed PRs | Still present |
| Optional test note | Still applies |

**Verified:** The locale fix is unchanged. All five `lpstat` calls still pin `LC_MESSAGES=C`. The reworded comment on lines 26-27 matches CUPS 2.4.19 (`cups/language.c`: in the C locale, `LC_MESSAGES` is read before `LC_ALL` and `LANG`, and `LANGUAGE` is never read).

### The CUPS-down check cannot read `printers.conf` as the migration user

The new check (line 36) runs `grep -q 'implicitclass://' /etc/cups/printers.conf 2>/dev/null` without `sudo`. Migrations run as the regular user: `bin/omarchy-migrate` runs each file without `sudo`, `omarchy update` calls it as the user, and `agents/skills/migrations.md` says so directly. On Arch `cups` 2:2.4.19-1, cupsd makes `printers.conf` root-owned with mode 0600 at every start and whenever it saves queues. So grep gets "Permission denied" and exits 2, `2>/dev/null` hides the message, and the `if` treats it like "no match".

Isolated runs with every privileged, package, systemd and CUPS command stubbed, and `lpstat -v` returning `lpstat: Scheduler is not running.`:

```text
case                                                  exit  cups-browsed dropped  marker written
head, readable printers.conf with implicitclass://    1     no                    no      (positive control)
head, unreadable printers.conf with implicitclass://  0     yes                   yes
head, readable printers.conf with ipp:// only         0     yes                   yes     (negative control)
prior head f8bb0162, readable with implicitclass://   0     yes                   yes
```

The root-owned 0600 file was modelled with a file the test user cannot open. Ownership and mode on real systems come from the CUPS source and Arch packaging, not from a live system.

**Impact:**
- On a real system this branch behaves as at the prior head: saved `implicitclass://` queues are never examined, cups-browsed is dropped and the machine marker prevents a later retry.
- The header comment (lines 23-25, "every other failure keeps the migration pending") and the new branch comment (lines 33-35, "retry rather than mark the migration complete") describe a retry that does not happen. The header comment stays inaccurate even with a working check, since scheduler-down with no saved queue still completes, so it needs updating either way.

**Suggested change (untested):**
- Read the file with privilege, as the migration already does for its other steps, for example `if sudo grep -qs '^DeviceURI implicitclass://' /etc/cups/printers.conf; then`. Anchoring on `DeviceURI` also avoids matching an `Info` description that mentions `implicitclass://`.
- Once the check works, a failed migration stops `omarchy update` before its later steps, and "retry later" fails the same way for as long as CUPS stays off. Naming the action would help, for example "Start CUPS (sudo systemctl start cups.service) and run the update again." With `cups.socket` enabled, as in Omarchy's default setup, systemd starts the scheduler when `lpstat` connects, so this branch is mainly reached when both the service and the socket are off.

### Open PR #12503 no longer conflicts, but would disable the new check

At `f8bb0162` a three-way merge with #12503 conflicted in the `elif`. At `4d2ea3d0` it merges cleanly in both orders. #12503 (head `5bbf8bbd`) adds `lpstat: Scheduler is not running.` to the first `elif`, which sets `queue_report=""`. In the merged file that branch comes first, so this PR's CUPS-down branch becomes unreachable and scheduler-down completes unconditionally again.

**Impact:** Merging both PRs gives no conflict to flag the overlap, and the retry added here would silently stop running.

**Suggested change:** Maintainers will likely want only one of the two. If both land, the scheduler-down alternative in #12503's condition needs to go.

**Description (still present):** The body still cites #9406 and #9650, which are closed PRs. The issues are #9377 and #9640 (`Fixes #9377` and `Fixes #9640` would close them on merge). The first bullet ("Treat "Scheduler is not running" like an empty queue") no longer describes the intended head behaviour, which is to retry when saved discovery queues exist.

**Optional test improvement (still applies):** No repository test covers this migration. A test of the new branch would need an unreadable `printers.conf`. A readable fixture passes while real systems skip the check, as the first two rows above show.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the migration at head `4d2ea3d0` against the prior head `f8bb0162`, the base and the current quattro tip (the file is unchanged there), plus `bin/omarchy-migrate`, CUPS 2.4.19, Arch `cups` 2:2.4.19-1 packaging and cups-browsed 2.1.1. Isolated runs of the head, prior and base migrations (the head as a copy with the `printers.conf` path pointed at a synthetic file) used stubbed privileged, package, systemd and CUPS commands and a stubbed `lpstat`. Root-owned `printers.conf` permissions were modelled, not observed. No real `lpstat` or `cupsd` ran in this follow-up; the locale behaviour rests on source and the earlier review's runs. Merge checks used #12503 at `5bbf8bbd`.

**AI process:** Fresh follow-up review: Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
